title: Field-extension transitions compose.
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an arbitrary scheme $X$, with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$ be finite intermediate extensions, with rings of integers as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $A_K=K_X$ and $R_K=\mathcal O_{K,X}$ for the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $a_K:R_K\to A_K$ for [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], for $K=E,F,H$. Write $c_{KL}:A_K\to A_L$ for the field inclusions [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map], $r_{KL}:R_K\to R_L$ for the uniquely characterized integral maps of [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique], and $q_{KL,n}:B_{K,n}\to B_{L,n}$ for the uniquely characterized quotient maps of [lem-route-sp-ell-map-exists-unique], where $B_{K,n}=(\mathcal O_K/\ell^{n+1})_X$ and $d_{K,n}:R_K\to B_{K,n}$ is reduction.

Let $M_n=\mu_{\ell^{n+1},X}$, with its power transitions [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Form $L_K=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(B_{K,n}\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}M_n)$ in $R_K$-modules, with transitions reduction on $B$ tensored with the power map on $M$, and let $p_{K,n}$ be its projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $u_{KL}:L_K\to L_L$ be the unique morphism of underlying abelian sheaves satisfying $p_{L,n}\circ u_{KL}=(q_{KL,n}\otimes1)\circ p_{K,n}$ for all $n$ [lem-route-sp-integral-twist-map-exists-unique]. Put $T_K=A_K\otimes_{R_K}L_K$, with the defining tensor quotient $e_K:A_K\otimes_{\mathbf Z_X}L_K\to T_K$. Let $j_{KL}:T_K\to T_L$ be the unique morphism of abelian sheaves with
$$j_{KL}\circ e_K=e_L\circ(c_{KL}\otimes u_{KL})$$
as in [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique]. Then these specified rational transitions compose:
$$j_{EH}=j_{FH}\circ j_{EF}.$$
This is the equality of underlying abelian-sheaf morphisms denoted by $\mathrm{spRationalTwistMap}\ X\ \ell\ (h.\mathrm{trans}\ k)=\mathrm{spRationalTwistMap}\ X\ \ell\ h\;\gg\;\mathrm{spRationalTwistMap}\ X\ \ell\ k$ for $h:E\leq F$ and $k:F\leq H$. No invertibility hypothesis on $\ell$ on $X$ is needed for this composition assertion.

proof.text: The condensed inclusions compose by the strict functoriality in [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map]. Their pullbacks therefore give $c_{FH}\circ c_{EF}=c_{EH}$: coefficient change is application of the inverse-image functor [def-sfb-coefficient-map, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. By [lem-route-sp-integers-map-exists-unique] the maps $r_{KL}$ preserve the ring structure and satisfy $a_Lr_{KL}=c_{KL}a_K$. Consequently $a_Hr_{FH}r_{EF}=c_{FH}a_Fr_{EF}=c_{FH}c_{EF}a_E=c_{EH}a_E$. The composite of the two ring maps is a ring map, since it preserves unit and multiplication successively. Thus it satisfies both defining conditions for $r_{EH}$; the uniqueness clause of the same cited statement gives $r_{FH}r_{EF}=r_{EH}$.

proof.text: For each $n\geq0$, [lem-route-sp-ell-map-exists-unique] gives $q_{KL,n}d_{K,n}=d_{L,n}r_{KL}$. Hence $q_{FH,n}q_{EF,n}d_{E,n}=q_{FH,n}d_{F,n}r_{EF}=d_{H,n}r_{FH}r_{EF}=d_{H,n}r_{EH}$. The uniqueness clause, now for the pair $E\subseteq H$, gives $q_{FH,n}q_{EF,n}=q_{EH,n}$. In particular this argument does not assume the quotient inclusion is injective or that reduction is surjective on sections of every pro-etale object.

proof.text: Use the projection equations of [lem-route-sp-integral-twist-map-exists-unique]. At every $n$ they give $p_{H,n}u_{FH}u_{EF}=(q_{FH,n}\otimes1)p_{F,n}u_{EF}=(q_{FH,n}\otimes1)(q_{EF,n}\otimes1)p_{E,n}=(q_{EH,n}\otimes1)p_{E,n}$. The middle tensor identity follows from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: on the presheaf tensors both composites send $b\otimes m$ to $q_{FH,n}(q_{EF,n}(b))\otimes m$, hence agree on finite sums and after sheafification. Thus $u_{FH}u_{EF}$ satisfies precisely the equations characterizing $u_{EH}$; uniqueness in the cited integral-map statement gives $u_{FH}u_{EF}=u_{EH}$. No exactness or surjectivity of inverse limits is used.

proof.text: Apply the normalization equations of [lem-route-sp-rational-twist-map-exists-unique] successively. They give $(j_{FH}j_{EF})e_E=j_{FH}e_F(c_{EF}\otimes u_{EF})=e_H(c_{FH}\otimes u_{FH})(c_{EF}\otimes u_{EF})=e_H(c_{EH}\otimes u_{EH})$. For the last equality use the two identities already proved; tensor bifunctoriality here is the direct calculation $a\otimes t\mapsto c_{FH}(c_{EF}(a))\otimes u_{FH}(u_{EF}(t))$ on presheaf pure tensors, extended to sums and sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Therefore $j_{FH}j_{EF}$ satisfies the defining tensor equation for the pair $E\subseteq H$. The uniqueness clause of the rational-map statement implies $j_{FH}j_{EF}=j_{EH}$, which is the required equality. This compares morphisms via their tensor quotient, without assuming all sections of the sheafified tensor are pure tensors.

Step 1: the composite c_FH c_EF = c_EH comes from the strict functoriality in def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-map and from p_X^* being a functor (def-sfb-coefficient-map, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients); I checked a_H r_FH r_EF = c_EH a_E, that the composite is still a ring map, and the uniqueness in the integers node. Step 2: q_FH q_EF d_E = d_H r_EH, then uniqueness; no epi or injectivity claim is needed. Step 3: the projection equations hold for the composite, with (q tensor 1)(q tensor 1) = (q q) tensor 1 checked on presheaf pure tensors and passed through sheafification (def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product), then uniqueness. Step 4: the tensor normalization holds for the composite, using bifunctoriality and steps 1 and 3, then uniqueness through the tensor quotient; it does not assume sections are pure tensors. Each step is a few lines of substitution plus a cited uniqueness, so elementary:true is justified. There are no new nodes, and no cycle (I computed the 299 ancestors over stmt/proof/step deps; the item is not among them).
